overview.text: The Japanese Rat Snake ('aodaishō', the 'blue general') is a non-venomous snake found across most of Japan. It is the largest snake in Japan outside Okinawa.

identification.text: Pale yellow-green to dark blue-green, with a dark streak behind each eye.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Japan from Hokkaido to Kyushu and nearby islands, and Kunashir in the Kuril Islands.

behaviour.text: Partly a climber that raids birds' nests. It rests through the winter for three to four months. Eagles and raccoon dogs hunt it.

diet.text: Rodents, frogs, lizards, shrews, birds and eggs. Farmers liked it for controlling rats.

reproduction.text: Mates in spring and lays 7 to 20 eggs in early summer.

recognise.text: Greenish to blue-green with a dark streak behind the eye.
